title: Control plane resilience and rotation test matrix
content:
Purpose:
This is a working runbook + test matrix focused on control plane resilience, node rotations, KMS/key rotations, and upgrade/scale procedures for private deployments (VPC and on-prem). The goal is to capture repeatable steps, failure modes, verification checks, and Terraform-module-specific notes so field engineers and SREs can run safe maintenance windows.

Scope:
- Initial bootstrap sanity checks for a new private control plane (VPC or on-prem).
- Horizontal/vertical scaling scenarios and expected client-facing impact.
- Node/container rotations: kubelet/draining, service reconvergence, KV cache warmup expectations.
- Secrets/KMS rotation workflow and rollback considerations.
- Upgrade path for control-plane components with terraform module quirks documented.
- Test matrix with automated/manual verification steps.

Quick summary notes (TL;DR):
- Always run terraform plan and a dry-run apply in an isolated staging control plane before production.
- Prefer staggered rotations (one rack/node at a time) for on-prem. For VPC, prefer AZ-aware rotations.
- KV cache priming is critical after rotations; expect initial 2–5x latency bursts for 5–15 minutes depending on QPS.
- KMS rotation: rotate keys in the KMS provider first, then re-encrypt DB blobs using a single worker, validate reads, then promote.

Prerequisites and environment checklist:
- Access: bastion / VPN credentials, SRE sudo group, terraform cloud token, kubeconfig with cluster-admin.
- Inventory: node list (hostnames), rack/AZ mapping, GPU/CPU types, current model-serving pools and autoscaler config.
- Backups: latest etcd snapshot (if using etcd), full DB export, object-store backups for artifacts.
- Monitoring: Grafana dashboards, alerting runbook links, tracing hooks configured, and a low-latency metric for "controlplane-latency-p50/p95" visible.
- Communication: Slack channel prepped, incident bridge, customer notification template if impact >5% SLA.

Terraform module notes / gotchas (field notes):
- Modules referenced: rf-controlplane-core v1.14.x, rf-networking v2.2.x, rf-kms-integration v0.9.
- State locking: enforce remote state with DynamoDB locks (AWS) or GCS lock object. Confirm lock TTLs before running long ops.
- Provider version pinning: provider "aws" >= 4.45.0 to avoid ENI attachment revert bug.
- Common var pitfalls: avoid changing control_plane_subnet_cidrs in-place; replace via blue-green when necessary.
- Module outputs we rely on in ops: control_plane_endpoint, control_plane_lb_ips, kms_key_arn, node_pool_ids. Don't change output names across versions.
- Roll-forward strategy: when upgrading modules, use a feature-branch state copy in terraform cloud workspace to run full plan and smoke apply.

Initial setup checklist (first-time deployment):
1) Validate network: ensure customer VPC routes to bastion and control-plane subnet is NATed if necessary.
2) Confirm KMS integration: test Encrypt/Decrypt with sample payloads.
3) Apply infra modules: terraform init -> terraform plan (workspace: staging) -> terraform apply.
4) Provision control-plane services and wait for health-checks: curl -f https://{{control_plane_endpoint}}/healthz
5) Run post-provision acceptance: run qa/e2e suite with synthetic traffic at 5–10 qps for 10 minutes.

Scaling scenarios and recommended operational approach:
- Small scale-up (add 1–2 nodes to node pool): can be done with terraform apply targeting node_pool_count variable. Verify autoscaler sees new capacity. Expected impact: negligible.
- Large scale-up ( >25% capacity): perform in waves of 10–15% increments, monitor scheduling latency and token service heatmaps.
- Vertical scale (node type change): create new node pool with desired instance type, cordon+drain old nodes, delete old pool after traffic stabilizes.
- Burst handling: enable short-term burst pool (pre-warmed spot/ephemeral) via tf var burst_pool_enabled=true. Ensure fallback policy to parked-models is configured.

Rotation runbook (nodes):
- Trigger: security patch, kernel upgrade, hardware replacement.
- Steps:
  a) Select target node (prefer: lowest pod density, not model-serving hot node).
  b) kubectl cordon <node>
  c) kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300 --timeout=10m
  d) Wait for pod reschedules and model cache warms (verify controlplane-metrics: model-cache-hit-rate)
  e) Run smoke test: generate 3 short requests and 3 long requests; check p95 < SLA threshold.
  f) Deprovision node via terraform (taint + apply) or replace hardware, then uncordon new node if reprovisioned.
- Verification: no pod restarts outside the node being rotated, API error rate spike < 3x baseline and less than 1% of requests fail.
- Rollback: if reschedules fail or persistent failures, reintroduce the previous node by uncordoning, or reroute traffic to dedicated region.

Rotation runbook (KMS/secrets):
- Prep: ensure an out-of-band key backup and at-rest archived keys exist.
- Sequence:
  1) Create new key version in KMS (do NOT disable old key yet).
  2) Staged re-encryption: run a single-worker job to re-encrypt database blobs with new key and write to new column "enc_v2".
  3) Validate reads from enc_v2 for 1000 sample records.
  4) Flip flag in config: secrets_key_version = "v2" via feature flag.
  5) Roll out config change to control-plane pods slowly (1 pod at a time).
  6) Monitor decrypt failures and API error rate for 30m.
  7) Decommission old key after 7 days (to allow rollback window).
- Gotcha: some legacy components still call KMS directly (check rf-legacy-migrator service); add compatibility shim if needed.

Upgrade plan (control-plane software):
- Strategy: canary -> staggered -> full. For infra module upgrades do module-specific staging workspace apply first.
- Steps:
  1) Branch + bump module versions in infra repo, open PR with terraform plan output.
  2) Apply to staging workspace, run full e2e and load soak for 2h at expected traffic profile.
  3) If green, schedule a maintenance window and apply to production in 3 waves (10%, 40%, 100%).
  4) Post-apply verification: run A/B traffic tests comparing previous pool vs new pool, check latencies and cost metrics.
  5) Rollback path: re-run terraform apply with previous module version. Keep plan outputs archived.
- Notes: ephemeral LB IP changes are expected on some module upgrades. Ensure DNS TTLs are low before upgrade to reduce cutover latency.

Test matrix (high-level) - execute before/after every maintenance window:
- Test case: APIZ health check
  - Type: automated
  - Trigger: post-apply
  - Steps: curl health endpoint x10
  - Expected: 200 OK; <1% 500s observed
- Test case: KV cache priming latency
  - Type: load test
  - Trigger: after node rotations
  - Steps: ramp qps from 0 to 50 for 10m
  - Expected: p95 returns to baseline within 20 minutes
- Test case: KMS rotate integrity
  - Type: integration
  - Trigger: after key flip
  - Steps: read/write 1000 records via migration worker
  - Expected: 0 decrypt failures
- Test case: Terraform drift detect
  - Type: config
  - Trigger: weekly cron
  - Steps: run terraform plan in read-only workspace
  - Expected: no unexpected diffs; any diff -> create ticket

Monitoring and alerting checks to verify after changes:
- controlplane-cpu-utilization per node (look for >85% sustained)
- request_error_rate (5m) and request_latency_p95 (1m)
- model-cache-hit-rate and kv-cache-miss-rate
- kube-scheduler queue length and pod evictions
- etcd commit latency (if applicable)

Failure scenarios and run actions:
- Scenario: apply fails and state is partially updated
  - Action: pause; do not re-apply. Export current state snapshot, create isolated workspace with that state, run plan to see corruption, roll back using archived plan.
- Scenario: API error spike after rotation
  - Action: throttle new traffic with feature flag, uncordon old nodes if available, escalate to SRE on-call.
- Scenario: KMS decrypt failures
  - Action: switch back to old key by flipping secrets_key_version flag, alert security and stakeholders, halt planned rotations.

Operational checklist (pre-maintenance):
- Run terraform fmt and validate modules locally.
- Confirm state lock and backup state file.
- Post a maintenance note in #priv-deployments with expected timeline.
- Disable automated scaling if doing large-scale node replacements.
- Snapshot DB and backup artifact store.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Add automated job to prime model KV cache after node replacement (reduce manual verification).
- Define explicit SLA thresholds for rotation windows per customer tier.
- Improve terraform regression tests to capture subtle output-name changes across module versions.
- Validate compatibility with on-prem HSM (customer-specific) for key rotation plan.

References and links:
- Confluence: CP terraform modules (linked above)
- GitHub: infra repo PRs that touched modules (see linked_artifacts)
- Runbooks: incident-handling and customer-notification templates

Revision history:
- 2024-11-03: initial draft (Priya)
- 2024-12-10: added KMS rotation sequence (Alex)
- 2025-01-15: expanded test matrix and terraform gotchas (Diego)

End of doc.
